zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 開篇固定收益主論點

美國經濟活動數據強勁，使8月21日美債賣壓集中在對聯準會政策較敏感的天期。2年期殖利率上升4.7個基點至4.237%，升幅超過10年期的2.9個基點；後者收在4.735%。30年期上升2.3個基點至5.272%。財政部擴大債券買回的首週，最終未能留下持續的債市漲勢；不過，週五直接推高殖利率的是成長與實質殖利率，而非通膨補償再度上升。

標普全球指標顯示，美國企業活動以逾4年來最快速度擴張。雖然近期就業、零售銷售與基礎通膨數據較弱，這項結果仍使升息可能性不能排除。10年期實質殖利率上升4.8個基點至2.402%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則下降1.9個基點至2.333%。油價仍上漲：布蘭特原油收在每桶$94.39，單日漲0.65%、全週漲6.63%。週五利率市場的反應因此有別於週四由通膨帶動的賣壓，但能源風險尚未消退。

其他市場也呈現分歧。標普500指數上漲0.43%，那斯達克100指數上漲0.33%，VIX降至15.13；半導體指數卻下跌0.51%，全週跌5.45%，反映投資人仍在衡量AI建設成本。黃金期貨上漲2.39%至$4,624.10，美元指數下跌0.10%至98.8。投資人可以同時看好經濟活動與企業獲利，要求持有政府長天期債券取得更高補償，並質疑舉債支持的成長須付出多大代價。

資金競爭不限於美債。新的資料中心融資報導顯示，投資等級專案以超過7%的殖利率吸引高收益債投資人；參與Alphabet澳洲市場創紀錄發債的投資人則提醒，當地每年只能承接少數幾筆同等規模交易。歐洲薪資與通膨預期數據緩和了歐洲央行眼前的疑慮，南韓出口強勁則加深南韓央行的緊縮討論。至於困境債權，法院對資產的控制權及擬議救援融資的條件，比當日整體市場的風險偏好更攸關結果。

## 經濟活動強勁，短天期美債重新定價

週五美債殖利率曲線轉為趨平，逆轉前一交易日的陡峭化。彭博按日殖利率資料顯示，5年期殖利率上升3.4個基點至4.425%，升幅介於2年期與更長天期之間。2年期與10年期利差收窄1.8個基點至49.8個基點；2年期與30年期利差收窄2.4個基點至103.5個基點。不過，單日趨平沒有消除較長期間持有長天期債券成本上升的變化：過去1個月，30年期殖利率上升13.9個基點，2年期反而下降2.7個基點。

標普全球的企業活動結果，為當日短天期領跌提供了經濟層面的解釋。企業成長加快，使聯準會較難僅憑其他較弱數據，就淡化通膨高於目標的問題，但這不代表再次升息已成定局。週五債市報導引述的交換市場定價顯示，9月升息機率約40%，直到接近年底才反映完整一次升息。7月政策會議有3名成員主張升息，隨後較弱的就業、零售銷售與基礎通膨數據，仍壓抑市場對立即行動的預期。

實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率的走勢，進一步說明週五與週四的差別。週四原油上漲時，名目公債遭拋售，通膨補償也上升；週五損益兩平通膨率下降，令10年期實質殖利率升幅超過名目殖利率。紐約收盤時布蘭特與WTI原油都上漲，其中WTI漲0.26%至每桶$87.06，但利率市場沒有延續週四的通膨重新定價。企業活動強勁，是短天期領跌更直接的解釋。

財政部長貝森特的債市介入措施，仍是投資人面對的另一項要事。財政部週三宣布，將把部分較長天期債券的買回規模至少提高一倍，殖利率起初下降，週四卻反彈；至週五收盤，10年期接近4.74%，30年期高於5.27%。貝森特表示買回規模可能進一步擴大，並承諾提出針對高借款成本的財政措施。川普總統週五說，介入決定由貝森特自行作出，並非他指示採取的行動。

市場關切的是，改變債務期限結構與減少借款是兩回事。貝森特所稱的「財政部扭轉操作」，以增加短天期融資支應長債買回，可減少民間投資人須承接的長天期利率風險，但政府仍須為赤字籌資。荷蘭合作銀行策略師Philip Marey警告，轉向短債最終會受到債務上限約束。他也提出一種情境：若殖利率再度承壓，市場可能要求聯準會買債；這是他的推演，並非央行宣布的計畫。

投資人也在評估財政部是否會控制未來最長天期債券的發行。近期季度發債聲明的措辭變動，引發這類猜測。Western Asset投資組合經理Robert Abad認為，若進一步買回，或改變長天期發行安排，就更能表明官員回應的不只是市場運作，也包括殖利率水準。財政部稱買回旨在支持舊券流動性；摩根大通利率策略師則指出，今年市場運作已明顯改善。分歧在於措施的目的及效果能否持久，而非週五殖利率是否上升。

財政承諾還須面對債務存量與持續赤字。本週美國公共債務突破$40兆，赤字規模接近$2兆。貝森特說，他將與白宮預算主任Russ Vought檢視收入與支出，並提及詐欺及對各州的移轉支付。Evercore ISI策略師Sarah Bianchi懷疑政府能在短期內大幅削減赤字，理由是支出路徑所繫的主要社會福利計畫在政治上難以更動。截至週五收盤，政府尚未宣布量化的借款縮減目標。

長期資金需求也不全由財政部決定。貝森特認為，AI企業預期建設將帶來高報酬，因此對殖利率相對不敏感，並建議它們考慮增加約5年期的發債。巴克萊策略師則把大型雲端運算業者借款列為長天期利率壓力的來源之一。各國政府同時為國防、能源與社會計畫籌資。財政部能調整自身債務期限，影響特定天期的債券供給，卻無法消除與其爭奪資金的其他融資需求。

週五現券交易較前一日平靜。FINRA記錄的美債面額成交量為$9,797億，較週四下降21.4%；其中附息名目公債為$8,324億，下降18.1%。剩餘期限超過20年的債券成交量下降35.8%至$885億。這些數字是雙向成交量，顯示在最初介入及隨後行情逆轉帶來的大量交易之後，殖利率繼續上升，成交量則回落。

貨幣與另類資產也反映壓力，但訊號並不一致。美元指數全週下跌0.87%，黃金期貨同期上漲5.56%。布魯金斯學會的Robin Brooks把壓抑殖利率的努力與日本曾經出現的貨幣疲弱相比；南非標準銀行的Steven Barrow則認為，買回會拖累美元，卻無法解決根本的赤字問題。不過，財政部透過債務管理融資的買回，有別於日本央行為壓低殖利率而大規模買債。美元指數週五僅跌0.10%，相較黃金與比特幣的全週漲幅，單日變動有限。

比特幣漲勢另有可辨識的推力。週五盤中漲幅一度達9.4%；彭博引述Coinglass數據顯示，約$25億的比特幣空頭部位在3天內遭強制平倉。美國上市的比特幣現貨基金全週流入超過$10億。川普總統與加密貨幣業主管會面，並再次呼籲國會通過《Clarity Act》，也構成另一項政策催化因素。漲勢可能反映財政與貨幣疑慮，但空頭回補及基金流入影響了上漲速度。

股票市場較樂於接受強勁的企業活動訊號。標普500指數上漲0.43%，那斯達克100指數上漲0.33%，後者結束連跌5天；兩項指數全週仍下跌。半導體指數續跌，使融資及估值問題在大盤反彈中依然顯眼。信用債基金價格漲跌幅都小：LQD跌0.13%，HYG、JNK與EMB則各自小幅上漲。當日最明顯的固定收益重新定價，仍在美債的政策敏感天期與實質殖利率。

## AI債務找到買家，融資價格卻更高

新的資料中心融資報導說明，市場強烈希望參與AI投資，並未讓相關專案取得廉價債務。QTS Realty Trust為喬治亞州一處與微軟相關的設施發行$39億債券，雖具投資等級評級，殖利率仍約7.23%。貝萊德為德州資料中心專案發行的投資等級證券，7月出售時殖利率為7.53%。知情人士表示，承銷商將這兩筆交易配售給投資等級與高收益債投資人。

QTS交易先前已確立該專案的融資價格；新資訊在於這類債券形成了怎樣的買方群。通常與較弱信用債相關的殖利率，吸引投機等級債經理人參與投資等級交易，擴大大型發債案的承接範圍，也顯示投資人要求多少補償，才願意在預期現金流實現前，承擔多年建設、租戶與再融資風險。同一報導指出，甲骨文與SpaceX的高評級票據，也曾以較常見於垃圾債的殖利率交易。

彭博彙整數據顯示，企業今年已為資料中心及其他AI投資借入超過$4,100億。Vanguard估計，大型雲端運算業者2026年支出可能接近$8,000億，2027年至2030年每年超過$1兆，且大部分支出將透過債市籌資。這些是未來投資與融資估計，並非已售出的債券。龐大的發債規劃使每筆新交易都須放在後續供給的背景下定價：投資人承接眼前專案風險，也得衡量還會有多少類似債券進入市場。

高收益債買家能增加承接能力，但其市場規模較小。美國垃圾債市場約$1.5兆，不及投資等級債市場的五分之一。若這些投資人要大幅增持投資等級AI債，可能須在流動性較低的市場賣出既有部位。摩根士丹利策略師預期，利差上升會先限制評級較低的AI借款人。財力最強的科技公司可在等待投資回報時負擔昂貴融資；較小企業及專案在融資成本與日後收入之間的緩衝較少。

Alphabet的澳洲交易，從另一個市場呈現籌資管道與承接能力。其首次發行的A$55億債券，是當地規模最大的公司債交易，收到超過A$180億訂單。今年外國借款人已發行超過A$640億澳幣債。澳洲大型退休基金提供本地需求，跨幣別交換則讓發行人把募集資金換成所需貨幣。彭博彙整數據顯示，Alphabet的20年期澳幣債在換回美元後，定價大致相當於其美國借款成本。

參與交易的昆士蘭投資公司（QIC）提醒，不能把Alphabet所受歡迎的程度推及所有大型雲端運算業者。QIC原投標A$3億，最後跨各券別買入約A$1.7億。固定收益策略主管Marayka Ward預期會有更多大型科技公司在澳洲發債，但認為當地市場每年只能容納約兩筆如此規模的交易。她也指出，需求因發行人而異：QIC認為Alphabet債券相對於澳洲銀行債有吸引力，卻懷疑Meta發債能在其投資組合中得到同樣反應。

澳幣債市場擴大，也使避險需求與初級市場發行一同增加。週四近月3年期澳洲政府公債期貨未平倉量達140萬口，是2019年5月以來最高，接近2008年創下的143萬口紀錄。澳幣債券市值從2022年10月低點至本月上升近40%，達A$2.14兆。澳洲國民銀行利率策略師Ken Crompton認為，市場規模擴大使政府與公司債的避險需求穩步增加。期貨部位顯示有多少曝險需要管理，卻無法據此判斷持有人預期殖利率升降。

這些交易使主權借款人面對的資金競爭有了更具體的價格。Alphabet能跨幣別分散融資並吸引大量訂單；資料中心專案也能觸及傳統投資等級債買家以外的投資人，但兩者都不代表市場可按以往的融資成本無限承接。對發行人與投資人而言，擔保、租戶、抵押品及重複發債將如何分攤融資負擔，愈來愈重要。

## 政策數據使各國殖利率曲線走向分歧

歐元區數據讓歐洲央行看到國內價格壓力放緩的跡象，儘管整體通膨仍接近3%。第2季協商薪資年增2.44%，低於前季修正後的2.56%，也遠低於2024年的5.55%高峰。歐洲央行密切觀察薪資，以判斷能源成本上升是否經由薪資傳導至更廣泛的通膨。其薪資追蹤指標仍顯示增速可能持續加快至2027年初，但幅度遠低於先前高峰。

另一項歐洲央行調查顯示，7月消費者預期未來1年物價上漲2.9%，低於6月的3%；3年期預期從2.8%降至2.7%。調查在7月2日至27日進行，期間美國與伊朗達成協議的前景及衝突再度升級，牽動能源價格。受訪者並預期歐元區經濟未來1年萎縮1.2%，較6月預測的萎縮1.4%緩和。通膨預期下降，減輕了政策制定者對二輪效應的部分疑慮；其水準仍高於2%目標，討論因此尚未結束。

歐洲央行管理委員會成員、拉脫維亞央行總裁Martins Kazaks明確表達了這種有條件的立場。他說，約3%的通膨令人不安，央行已準備好採取行動使其回到目標；但9月是否再升息，正反兩方面都有理由，不能預先判定。他一方面提到第2季成長優於預期、失業率低，另一方面指出薪資逐漸放緩、通膨預期在他看來仍受控制。市場在6月首次升息後，幾乎已反映再升息25個基點；Kazaks表示，決定仍取決於更新數據與前景。

瑞士面對的通膨情況截然不同。瑞士央行理事Petra Tschudin說，若有必要讓中期通膨維持在0%至2%的範圍，央行會把利率降至零以下。瑞士央行去年將政策利率降至零後一直維持不變；即使全球能源價格上漲，7月通膨仍放緩至0.4%。Tschudin表示，負利率與正利率的作用不同，須納入考量，但不妨礙央行使用負利率。第2季成長優於預期及薪資上升，使評估更複雜；她保留的是政策選項，並未宣布即將降息。

南韓新公布的貿易數據強化了進一步緊縮的理由，也顯示成長高度集中。8月前20天，按工作日調整的出口較上年同期增加61.5%；7月相應期間最初公布的增幅為62.9%。未調整出口增加56%，進口增加19%，貿易順差接近$140億。半導體出口激增198.8%，電腦相關產品增加242.1%，汽車出口則減少約45%。

對中國出口增加118.6%，對美國增加59.4%，對香港及越南分別增加245.5%和67.4%。晶片需求帶來可觀的對外貿易收益，汽車出口下滑卻說明成長並不全面。南韓央行7月將基準利率提高25個基點至2.75%，並維持緊縮傾向。當月整體通膨放緩至2.8%，核心通膨卻加快至2.6%；第2季產出較前季成長0.6%，優於預期。下週會議將顯示官員是否認為經濟足以支撐連續第二次升息，或希望有更多時間評估7月行動。

日本即將提出的預算請求，則為貨幣政策討論增添財政面向。明年4月開始的新財政年度，各部會請求總額預料將超過先前¥122兆的紀錄。據《讀賣新聞》報導，財務省正考慮以暫定利率3.8%估算下年度債務償付成本；本年度最初假設為2.6%。償債支出已占本年度預算約四分之一，更高的利率假設使JGB殖利率上升對支出安排更有影響。

預算請求總額仍須審慎解讀。首相高市早苗希望把經常性支出從追加預算移入初始預算；去年的追加預算規模為¥18.3兆。各部會還可透過獨立的多年期架構，為為期14年、規模¥370兆的成長策略提出不設上限的資本投資請求。被認定攸關經濟安全的投資，則會透過專戶，以有指定資金來源支持的過渡性債券融資。各部會預計下週開始提交請求；實際借款需求須待年底前後的最終預算與發債計畫才會更清楚。既有支出提前列入初始預算，會推高與上年相比的總額；較高的利息假設與新增承諾，同時也構成實際融資壓力。

## 困境債權取決於資產控制與新增資金

中國大陸法院週四判處恆大創辦人許家印無期徒刑並下令沒收其資產，使恆大境外債權人面臨新的難題。其旗下公司合計被罰人民幣158億元，約$24億。清盤人估計恆大債務約$450億，正設法追索許家印在全球約$77億資產；這項判決使大陸執法程序與清盤人的追索行動相遇。

境外債權最終能收回多少，仍未有定論。中國法律通常將損失賠償及債務償還置於罰款和沒收之前，但破產專家質疑，在不同司法管轄區及相互競爭的程序間，這項原則如何落實。香港清盤人對許家印的訴訟尚未勝訴，大陸命令能否及於境外財產，也可能取決於當地法院。判決後，多數境外債券變動不大，報價仍低於面值的2%。德勤2023年的清盤估計認為，美元票據平均可收回面值的3.4%；新判決改變了債權人可能需要採取的追索途徑，並未確立新的回收金額。

清盤人還在挑戰一項設立少數股東補償基金的10億港元安排，香港法院本週開始審理。這項爭議與大陸的資產沒收令涉及不同請求權，但在恆大重組失敗、2024年被下令清盤後，兩者都關係到可用資產的範圍與分配。

巴西石化公司Braskem面臨更迫近的決定。公司表示，與債權人的磋商加快，並已收到涉及注資及以資產提供擔保的初步、無約束力提案；截至週四晚間申報時仍未達成協議。法院下令的債權執行暫停保護將於8月24日到期，公司須爭取庭外安排，或考慮進入司法重整程序。

依巴西庭外重組制度，Braskem須取得持有至少三分之一債務的債權人支持，才能達成重組安排；達到門檻後，各方還有90天敲定條款。包括Elliott Investment Management與Contrarian Capital Management在內的債權人，要求與IG4 Capital Group共同控制Braskem的巴西石油公司Petrobras作出財務承諾。討論中的方案包括股權、營運資金或次順位債務；Petrobras也評估改善部分合約的付款條件。在選舉年，由誰負擔救援成本因此具有政治影響。

壓力已蔓延至Braskem的墨西哥子公司Braskem Idesa，後者本週在美國申請預先協商的破產保護。Braskem於2031年到期的美元債殖利率約23%；由於談判仍未解決，股價週五在聖保羅一度下跌4.5%。在暫停執行保護到期前，債權人能否取得足夠的新資金、擔保及股東支持，將決定其信用狀況下一步如何演變。

## 週末進展延續政策討論

週五固定收益市場收盤後，明尼阿波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari於週日直接談及債市賣壓。他表示，美債市場運作良好，交易與流動性足以讓聯準會繼續以聯邦基金利率作為對抗通膨的主要工具。Kashkari是7月主張升息25個基點的3名投票成員之一，仍不相信通膨會很快回到目標；但他沒有承諾9月再升息，表示希望看到更多數據。他的發言沒有影響週五價格，卻闡明了這名7月異議成員的看法：高殖利率既不表示市場失靈到需要聯準會介入，也不足以使他放下通膨疑慮。

高盛週末的評估，為中國是否需要寬鬆政策增添新的成長估計。中國首席經濟學家Hui Shan估計，第3季初GDP年增率約4%，低於前季的4.3%，也低於北京設定的全年4.5%至5%目標。她認為7月工業產出、消費及投資疲弱，源於需求不足。麥格理估計成長約4.2%，法國巴黎銀行估計為4.1%；後者指出，即使財政力度加大，若8月和9月成長維持在4%上下或更低，全年目標可能受威脅，並促使政府於9月下旬或10月初推出新刺激措施。

這些是經濟學家的估計，並非新發布的官方GDP數據；它們使最新評估超越了先前對7月活動疲弱的觀察。高盛指出，市場對貨幣寬鬆的預期有所升高，但中國著重科技與製造業，對家庭收入及消費的提振可能較有限。先前油價與出廠價格通膨上升，使許多分析師撤回降息預測。7月分析師預測中位數仍認為今年及明年都不會降政策利率，第4季調降銀行存款準備金率則較有可能。官員迄今討論的是貸款補貼與其他定向融資支持，並非廣泛寬鬆。

新興市場報酬也提供觀察近期美元疲弱的另一個角度。彭博追蹤8種主要新興市場貨幣的指標，自2024年底以來報酬約22%；以美元融資的利差交易已連續7季獲利，是2008年以來最長紀錄。不過，各國匯率貢獻差異很大：哥倫比亞同時提供高利息收益及披索明顯升值；土耳其里拉兌美元雖貶值26%，10年期本幣債超過32%的殖利率仍使投資人獲利。這些比較描述的是跨數季交易，並非對週五美債行情的反應。

主要風險是美國政策路徑轉趨緊縮，推高美元並侵蝕以當地貨幣取得的報酬。美元指數全週雖然下跌，週五2年期美債殖利率上升仍使這項風險更迫近。高盛策略師Kamakshya Trivedi認為，只要美國長天期殖利率上升不過快，高實質利率可繼續支撐新興市場貨幣。其他人士則警告，擁擠部位可能放大行情逆轉。這說明美元單日小幅下跌也可能影響全球債券報酬，但不表示所有新興市場主權或信用風險同步改善。

北美貿易關係也在美國債市收盤後惡化。美國與加拿大談判於週五晚間破裂，華府隨後對價值數十億美元的加拿大商品課徵50%關稅。加拿大總理Mark Carney其後表示，加拿大將自9月8日起，對價值$200億的美國產品課徵反制關稅。這些較晚發生的進展不能解釋週五美債收盤，卻為下週評估美加兩國的成長與通膨，增加貿易及價格風險。

## 後市關注重點

貝森特週一的說明，將首先檢驗投資人本週區分債務管理與財政改善的依據。若支出、收入或預計借款有具體且持久的變化，擴大買回便有相應的財政措施。增加買回或改變期限配置，可影響長債供給；但除非承諾的措施改變赤字路徑，整體融資需求仍在。政府同時提出在經濟上孤立伊朗的計畫，將另由石油出口、支付及航運受到的影響檢驗：儘管伊朗總統Masoud Pezeshkian呼籲結束戰爭，布蘭特原油週五仍收於每桶$94.39。

週三公布的美國個人消費支出（PCE）數據，將檢驗週五實質殖利率上升、損益兩平通膨率下降的走勢。經濟學家預期，7月整體物價指數年增3.6%，為4個月來最小年增幅，經通膨調整的個人支出則幾乎不變。對於須在強勁企業活動與較弱就業、消費證據間權衡的聯準會，數據組成將很重要。週三另有第2季GDP修正值；週二公布7月新屋銷售，週五公布非農就業基準初步修正。

更重要的政策事件是聯準會主席Kevin Warsh週五首次以主席身分在傑克森霍爾發表主題演說。投資人將關注他如何評估持續通膨、偏高的長天期殖利率對經濟的抑制作用，以及財政部調整長天期債券供給時，聯準會如何運用市場訊號。Kashkari週日已表明一名7月異議成員認為債市運作正常、9月決定仍取決於數據；Warsh對央行整體政策反應方式的說明，可能同時影響預期利率路徑與長天期美債的不確定性溢價。

南韓央行在出口激增後於週四決議利率。日本各部會的預算請求，將開始顯示較大的初始預算與獨立投資架構會如何列示支出。中國後續活動數據，則將檢驗高盛估計約4%的成長速度，在定向財政支持下是否持續。信用市場方面，Braskem於8月24日的暫停執行期限，可能使無約束力提案轉為各方同意的談判途徑，或導向法院程序。AI融資市場接下來的大型專案與大型雲端運算業者發債，將顯示跨評級買家能否繼續以目前殖利率吸收供給，以及較小借款人能否負擔相同成本。
zh-TW.methodology_note: 除非另有註明，市場水準均以紐約收盤為準。利率資料採用彭博每日殖利率歷史序列；變動幅度與推算的殖利率曲線均使用相同日期序列。每日歷史資料未註明觀察時刻。

overall_summary.headline: 美國經濟活動強勁推升美債殖利率，政策敏感的短天期領跌
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國企業活動以逾4年來最快速度擴張，美債8月21日收低。2年期殖利率上升4.7個基點至4.237%，升幅超過10年期的2.9個基點；後者收在4.735%。10年期實質殖利率上升4.8個基點，損益兩平通膨率則下降1.9個基點，顯示週五主要由成長帶動，有別於週四由通膨帶動的賣壓。油價仍然上漲；財政部擴大買回債券的首週結束時，也未帶來持續的債市漲勢。

大盤上漲，半導體股卻下跌，反映市場仍擔心AI建設成本。殖利率超過7%的投資等級資料中心債吸引高收益債買家；參與Alphabet澳洲市場創紀錄發債的投資人則提醒，當地每年只能承接少數幾筆同等規模交易。這些融資需求，使投資人願意按目前殖利率提供多少長期資金的問題更加突出。
overall_summary.summary: 企業成長加快推升實質殖利率、使美債殖利率曲線趨平；財政部擴大買回仍未帶來持續漲勢，投資人同時衡量舉債支持AI成長的成本。

section_summaries.summary: 強勁的企業活動使週五美債賣壓集中於對聯準會政策敏感的天期，通膨補償卻下降。股市歡迎成長訊號，但半導體股走弱與AI借款成本偏高，顯示長期資金需求仍是疑慮。歐洲政策數據走勢分歧；困境債權的結果則取決於資產請求權與救援融資。

section_summaries.summary: 中國大陸法院下令沒收恆大創辦人許家印的資產後，境外債權人對資產追償仍面臨不確定性；判決未確立新的回收金額。Braskem收到涉及新資本及資產擔保的無約束力提案，但在8月24日暫停債權執行保護到期前，仍未達成協議。

section_summaries.section_title: 週末進展延續政策討論
section_summaries.summary: 週五收盤後，7月主張升息的聯準會官員Neel Kashkari表示，美債市場運作良好，9月是否升息仍須更多數據。高盛估計中國第3季初成長約4%，增添寬鬆政策討論。新興市場利差交易長期獲利，仍面臨美國政策轉趨緊縮的風險；美加貿易談判破裂，則為下週增加新的價格風險。這些較晚發生的進展都未影響週五美債價格。
貝森特週一的財政說明，將檢驗擴大買回是否有可信的借款計畫配合。週三的PCE數據，將檢驗強勁企業活動與較弱通膨、支出證據之間的取捨。聯準會主席Kevin Warsh週五在傑克森霍爾的演說，可能釐清央行如何衡量持續通膨與偏高的長天期殖利率。Braskem的保護期限、南韓央行決定及後續中國數據，則分別檢驗信用與全球政策前景。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries ended August 21 lower after a strong U.S. business-activity reading shifted the day’s selling toward maturities most sensitive to Federal Reserve policy. The 2-year yield rose 4.7 basis points to 4.237%, outpacing the 10-year’s 2.9-basis-point increase to 4.735%. The 30-year yield added 2.3 basis points to 5.272%. The move left the expanded Treasury buyback plan without a sustained rally to show for its first week, even as Friday’s immediate pressure came from growth and real yields rather than another rise in inflation compensation.

S&P Global’s gauges showed U.S. business activity expanding at its fastest pace in more than four years. That qualitative result strengthened the case for keeping a possible rate increase in view despite softer recent employment, retail-sales and underlying inflation readings. The 10-year real yield climbed 4.8 basis points to 2.402%, while the 10-year breakeven fell 1.9 basis points to 2.333%. Oil still gained: Brent closed at $94.39 a barrel, up 0.65% on the day and 6.63% over the week. Friday’s rates move was therefore different from Thursday’s inflation-led selloff, although the energy risk had not gone away.

The broader market offered a similarly divided account. The S&P 500 rose 0.43%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.33% and the VIX fell to 15.13. The semiconductor index declined 0.51%, however, and ended the week down 5.45% as investors weighed the cost of the artificial-intelligence buildout. Gold futures rose 2.39% to $4,624.10 and the Dollar Index slipped 0.10% to 98.8. Investors could still welcome strong activity and corporate earnings while demanding more compensation for government duration and questioning what debt-funded growth will cost.

That competition for capital extended well beyond Treasuries. New reporting on data-center finance showed investment-grade projects drawing high-yield buyers by offering yields above 7%, while an Australian investor in Alphabet’s record local bond sale cautioned that the market could absorb only a few transactions of that size each year. Separate European wage and inflation-expectations readings eased one central bank’s immediate concerns, and South Korean export strength reinforced another’s tightening debate. In distressed credit, court control over assets and the terms of proposed rescue financing mattered more than the day’s broad risk appetite.

## Strong Activity Reprices the Front End

The U.S. selloff reversed the curve steepening of the previous session. Bloomberg’s dated yield histories put the 5-year at 4.425%, up 3.4 basis points, between the larger 2-year move and the smaller increases farther out. The 2s10s spread narrowed 1.8 basis points to 49.8 basis points, and 2s30s narrowed 2.4 basis points to 103.5 basis points. Friday’s flattening did not erase the longer shift in the cost of duration: over 1 month, the 30-year yield was 13.9 basis points higher, while the 2-year was 2.7 basis points lower.

The S&P Global activity result gave that daily pattern a plausible economic driver. A faster pace of business growth leaves the Fed less room to dismiss above-target inflation on the strength of weaker releases elsewhere. It did not establish that another increase is certain. Swaps cited in Friday’s bond-market account implied around a 40% chance of a hike at the September meeting, with a full move priced only around year-end. The July policy meeting had produced three dissents in favor of tightening, but the subsequent softer labor, retail and underlying inflation readings continued to temper expectations for an immediate move.

The real-yield and breakeven split sharpens the distinction. Thursday’s nominal selloff had been accompanied by higher inflation compensation as crude rose. On Friday, the increase in the 10-year real yield exceeded the increase in the nominal yield because the breakeven declined. Brent and WTI both rose at the New York close—WTI gained 0.26% to $87.06—but the rates market did not extend Thursday’s inflation repricing. Strength in business activity supplied a more direct explanation for the front-end-led move.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s intervention remained the other major issue facing bond investors. Wednesday’s announcement that the department would at least double buybacks of selected longer-dated securities initially drove yields lower. They rebounded on Thursday, and Friday’s close put the 10-year near 4.74% and the 30-year above 5.27%. Bessent has indicated that purchases could expand further and promised a fiscal initiative aimed at high borrowing costs. President Donald Trump said Friday that the decision to intervene was Bessent’s own, rather than an action Trump had directed.

The distinction between changing debt maturities and reducing borrowing remains central to the market response. Bessent described a “Treasury twist” in which purchases of long debt would be financed by greater reliance on shorter maturities. That could reduce the amount of duration private investors must absorb, but the government would still need to fund its deficit. Rabobank strategist Philip Marey warned that a shift toward short debt would ultimately be constrained by the debt ceiling. He raised the possibility that renewed yield pressure could prompt calls for Fed purchases, though that was his scenario, not an announced central-bank plan.

Investors are also assessing whether Treasury might restrain future sales at the longest maturities. Changes to language in the recent quarterly issuance statement encouraged that speculation. Western Asset portfolio manager Robert Abad said further buybacks or a change in long-end issuance would be stronger evidence that officials were responding to the level of yields as well as market functioning. Treasury has described the repurchases as support for liquidity in older securities; JPMorgan rates strategists, meanwhile, reported that market functioning had improved notably this year. The disagreement concerns the purpose and durability of the operation, not whether Friday’s yields rose.

The promised fiscal initiative will have to address a larger stock-and-flow problem. U.S. public debt crossed $40 trillion during the week, and the deficit is running near $2 trillion. Bessent said he and White House budget director Russ Vought would examine revenue and spending, mentioning fraud and transfers to states. Evercore ISI strategist Sarah Bianchi doubted the administration could deliver material near-term deficit reduction, pointing to the political difficulty of changing the major entitlement programs behind much of the spending path. No quantified reduction in borrowing had been announced by Friday’s close.

Nor can Treasury determine the full demand for long-term capital. Bessent argued that AI companies were relatively insensitive to yields because they expected high returns from the buildout, and suggested they consider issuing more around the 5-year maturity. Barclays strategists identified hyperscaler borrowing as one source of pressure on long rates. Governments are also financing defense, energy and social programs. Treasury can shift the duration of its own debt and affect the securities available in particular maturities; it cannot remove the financing needs competing with those securities.

Friday’s cash trading showed a quieter adjustment than the preceding session. FINRA recorded $979.7 billion of Treasury par activity, down 21.4% from Thursday, including $832.4 billion of nominal coupons, down 18.1%. Activity in maturities beyond 20 years fell 35.8% to $88.5 billion. These are two-way turnover figures, but they establish that yields rose while volume receded from the heavier trading around the initial intervention and its reversal.

The pressure also appeared in currency and alternative assets, though the signals were not uniform. The Dollar Index ended the week down 0.87%; gold futures gained 5.56% over the same period. Robin Brooks of the Brookings Institution compared efforts to contain yields with Japan’s experience of currency weakness, while Standard Bank’s Steven Barrow argued that buybacks would weigh on the dollar without fixing the underlying deficit. The analogy has a material limit: Treasury repurchases financed through debt management are different from the large central-bank bond purchases Japan used to hold yields down. The Dollar Index was down 0.10% Friday, a modest daily move beside the much larger weekly gains in gold and Bitcoin.

Bitcoin’s rally had additional, identifiable drivers. It climbed as much as 9.4% intraday Friday, and roughly $2.5 billion of bearish Bitcoin positions were liquidated over three days, according to Coinglass data cited by Bloomberg. U.S.-listed spot Bitcoin funds drew more than $1 billion during the week. President Trump’s meeting with crypto executives and renewed call for Congress to pass the Clarity Act added a separate policy catalyst. The surge may reflect fiscal and currency concerns, but forced covering and fund inflows helped determine its speed.

Equities were more receptive to the strong activity reading. The S&P 500’s 0.43% gain and the Nasdaq 100’s 0.33% advance ended a five-day losing streak for the latter, although both indexes fell over the week. The semiconductor index’s further decline kept the financing and valuation question visible within the broader rebound. Credit-fund prices were mixed and small: LQD fell 0.13%, while HYG, JNK and EMB each edged higher. The day’s clearest fixed-income repricing was in Treasuries’ policy-sensitive and real-yield components.

## AI Debt Finds Buyers at a Higher Price

A new account of data-center financing showed why strong demand for AI exposure has not translated into cheap debt. QTS Realty Trust’s $3.9 billion bond sale for a Microsoft-linked facility in Georgia carried investment-grade ratings yet yielded about 7.23%. BlackRock’s investment-grade securities for a Texas data-center project yielded 7.53% when sold in July. Underwriters placed both transactions with high-grade and high-yield investors, according to people familiar with the deals.

The QTS sale itself had already established a price for the project. The further finding is about the buyer base forming around such debt: yields associated with weaker credits are bringing speculative-grade managers into investment-grade transactions. That broadens distribution for a large deal, while showing how much compensation investors seek for years of construction, tenant and refinancing exposure before projects deliver their expected cash flows. High-grade notes from Oracle and SpaceX have also traded at yields more commonly associated with junk debt, according to the same reporting.

Companies have borrowed more than $410 billion this year for data centers and other AI investment, Bloomberg-compiled data show. Vanguard estimates hyperscalers could spend almost $800 billion in 2026 and more than $1 trillion annually from 2027 through 2030, with most spending funded in debt markets. Those estimates describe prospective investment and financing, rather than bonds already sold. Their scale helps explain why each new transaction is priced in the context of a pipeline: investors accepting today’s project risk must also consider how much similar debt may follow.

High-yield buyers add capacity, but their market is smaller. The U.S. junk-bond market is about $1.5 trillion, less than one-fifth the size of the high-grade market. To fund a substantial move into investment-grade AI bonds, those investors may have to sell existing positions in a less liquid market. Morgan Stanley strategists expect rising spreads to constrain lower-rated AI borrowers first. The strongest technology companies can carry costly financing while waiting for returns; smaller firms and projects have less room between their funding cost and eventual revenue.

Alphabet’s Australian transaction supplied a separate measure of both access and capacity. Its A$5.5 billion debut sale was the largest corporate bond offering in that market and drew more than A$18 billion of orders. Foreign borrowers have sold more than A$64 billion of Australian-dollar bonds this year. Australia’s large pension funds provide a local pool of demand, while cross-currency swaps let issuers convert proceeds into the currency they need. Alphabet’s 20-year Australian bond priced broadly in line with its U.S. borrowing cost after swapping the proceeds back into dollars, according to Bloomberg-compiled data.

An investor in the deal nevertheless cautioned against extrapolating its reception to every hyperscaler. Queensland Investment Corporation bought about A$170 million across the tranches after bidding for A$300 million. Marayka Ward, its director of fixed-income strategy, expects more Big Tech issuance in Australia but thinks the market has room for only a couple of deals of that scale each year. She also said investor enthusiasm could differ by issuer: QIC viewed Alphabet’s bonds as attractive relative to domestic bank debt, but she doubted that a transaction from Meta would draw the same response in its books.

The growing Australian-dollar debt market is changing hedging demand alongside primary issuance. Open interest in the front-month 3-year government-bond futures contract reached 1.4 million on Thursday, its highest since May 2019 and close to the 1.43 million record set in 2008. The market value of Australian-dollar bonds rose almost 40% from its October 2022 low to A$2.14 trillion this month. National Australia Bank rates strategist Ken Crompton linked the larger market to a steady increase in hedging needs across government and corporate debt. The futures positions show the scale of exposure being managed, without identifying whether holders expect yields to rise or fall.

These developments put a more precise price on the capital competition facing sovereign borrowers. Alphabet could diversify across currencies and attract a large book; data-center projects could reach beyond traditional high-grade buyers. Neither result implies unlimited capacity at the previous cost of funding. For issuers and investors alike, the question is increasingly how guarantees, tenants, collateral and repeat issuance divide the financing burden.

## Policy Data Pull Global Curves in Different Directions

Euro-area releases offered the European Central Bank evidence of easing domestic price pressure even as headline inflation remained near 3%. Negotiated wages rose 2.44% from a year earlier in Q2, down from a revised 2.56% in the previous quarter and well below the 5.55% peak in 2024. The ECB watches pay closely for signs that higher energy costs are spreading through wages into broader inflation. Its wage tracker still points to some acceleration through early 2027, though at rates far below that earlier peak.

A separate ECB survey showed consumers in July expected prices to rise 2.9% over the following year, down from 3% in June. The 3-year expectation fell to 2.7% from 2.8%. The survey ran from July 2 to July 27, when shifting prospects for a U.S.-Iran settlement and renewed escalation moved energy prices. Respondents also expected the euro-area economy to contract 1.2% over the next year, compared with a 1.4% decline forecast in June. The lower inflation readings give policymakers some reassurance about second-round effects, while levels above the 2% target keep the debate open.

ECB Governing Council member Martins Kazaks made that conditional position explicit. The Latvian central-bank chief called inflation around 3% uncomfortable and said the bank was prepared to act to return it to target. He would not prejudge September’s meeting, citing both arguments for and against another increase. He pointed to stronger-than-expected Q2 growth and low unemployment alongside gradually slowing wages and inflation expectations he considered anchored. Markets were close to pricing a further quarter-point hike after June’s initial move, but Kazaks said the decision would depend on updated data and the outlook.

Switzerland faces a markedly different inflation problem. Swiss National Bank board member Petra Tschudin said the bank would lower rates below zero if needed to keep inflation within its 0% to 2% medium-term range. The SNB has held its policy rate at zero since cutting it there last year, and July inflation slowed to 0.4% despite the global energy rise. Tschudin said the different effects of negative and positive rates would have to be considered, but would not prevent their use. Faster-than-expected Q2 growth and rising wages complicate the assessment; her statement preserved a policy option rather than announcing an imminent cut.

In South Korea, a fresh trade release strengthened the case for further tightening while showing how concentrated the expansion is. Working-day-adjusted exports rose 61.5% from a year earlier in the first 20 days of August, compared with an initially reported 62.9% gain in the corresponding July period. Unadjusted shipments increased 56%, imports rose 19%, and the trade surplus approached $14 billion. Semiconductor exports jumped 198.8% and computer-related products rose 242.1%, while automobile shipments fell about 45%.

Exports to China gained 118.6%, those to the U.S. increased 59.4%, and shipments to Hong Kong and Vietnam rose 245.5% and 67.4%, respectively. Chip demand is producing a substantial external windfall, but the automobile decline prevents the numbers from being read as uniform strength. The Bank of Korea raised its benchmark by 25 basis points to 2.75% in July and kept a tightening bias. Headline inflation slowed to 2.8% that month while core inflation accelerated to 2.6%; Q2 output grew a stronger-than-expected 0.6% from the preceding quarter. Next week’s meeting will test whether officials see enough resilience for a second consecutive increase or want more time to assess July’s move.

Japan’s forthcoming budget requests add a fiscal dimension to its monetary-policy debate. Requests for the fiscal year beginning next April are expected to exceed the previous ¥122 trillion record. The Finance Ministry is considering a provisional interest rate of 3.8% for calculating next year’s debt-service cost, according to a Yomiuri report, against a 2.6% initial assumption for the current year. Servicing already accounts for about one-quarter of this year’s budget, so the higher assumption makes rising JGB yields consequential for the spending plan.

The headline total will require care in interpretation. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi wants to shift recurring spending from supplementary budgets into the initial budget; last year’s supplementary package totaled ¥18.3 trillion. Ministries can also request uncapped capital-investment funding tied to a ¥370 trillion growth strategy over 14 years through a separate multi-year framework. Investment deemed critical to economic security would pass through a special account financed with bridge bonds backed by dedicated funding sources. Ministries are expected to begin submitting requests next week, but the eventual borrowing need will become clearer only with the final budget and bond-issuance plan toward year-end. Moving existing spending into an earlier document can inflate a year-on-year comparison even as higher interest assumptions and new commitments create genuine funding pressure.

## Distressed Credit Turns on Asset Control and New Money

Evergrande’s offshore creditors encountered a new complication after a mainland Chinese court sentenced founder Hui Ka Yan to life in prison on Thursday and ordered his assets confiscated. His companies were fined a combined 15.8 billion yuan, about $2.4 billion. The ruling brings a mainland enforcement process into contact with liquidators’ efforts to pursue roughly $7.7 billion of Hui’s assets worldwide for a developer whose debt they put at about $45 billion.

The effect on offshore recoveries is unresolved. Chinese law generally gives compensation for losses and repayment of debt priority over fines and confiscation, but insolvency specialists questioned how that principle would operate across jurisdictions and competing proceedings. Hong Kong liquidators have yet to win their case against Hui, and enforcement of a mainland order over overseas property may depend on local courts. Most offshore bonds were little changed after the ruling, indicated below 2 cents on the dollar. Deloitte’s 2023 liquidation estimate put average recovery on the dollar notes at 3.4%; the new judgment changes the route creditors may have to take, without establishing a new recovery amount.

The liquidators are also contesting a HK$1 billion arrangement that set up a compensation fund for minority shareholders, with a Hong Kong court beginning to hear their challenge during the week. That dispute and the mainland confiscation order concern different claims, but both bear on the pool and allocation of assets available after the developer’s failed restructuring and 2024 liquidation order.

Braskem faced a nearer decision. The Brazilian petrochemicals company said creditor talks had intensified and that it had received indicative, nonbinding proposals involving a capital injection and security interests over assets. It had reached no agreement by its late-Thursday filing. A court-ordered shield against enforcement was due to expire on August 24, leaving the company to pursue an out-of-court arrangement or consider judicial recovery.

Under Brazil’s extrajudicial framework, Braskem needs support from holders of at least one-third of its debt to agree to a restructuring. Reaching that threshold would give the parties a further 90 days to finalize terms. Creditors including Elliott Investment Management and Contrarian Capital Management have sought a financial commitment from Petrobras, which controls Braskem alongside IG4 Capital Group. Proposals discussed have included equity, working capital or junior debt; Petrobras has also weighed improved payment terms on some contracts. Its role makes the allocation of rescue costs politically consequential in an election year.

The strain has spread to Braskem’s Mexican unit, Braskem Idesa, which filed for prepackaged U.S. bankruptcy protection during the week. Braskem’s dollar bonds due in 2031 yielded about 23%, and its shares fell as much as 4.5% in São Paulo on Friday after talks remained unresolved. The next change in its credit position depends on whether creditors obtain sufficient new money, collateral and shareholder support before the stay expires.

## Weekend Developments Extend the Policy Debate

After the Friday fixed-income close, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari addressed the bond selloff directly. Speaking Sunday, he said the Treasury market was functioning well, with trading and liquidity sufficient for the Fed to keep the federal funds rate as its primary tool against inflation. Kashkari was one of the three July voters who favored a 25-basis-point hike, and he remained unconvinced that inflation was heading back to target quickly. He stopped short of committing to another increase in September, saying he wanted more data. His remarks did not drive Friday’s prices; they clarified that this July dissenter sees high yields neither as market dysfunction requiring Fed action nor as a reason to set aside his inflation concern.

A weekend Goldman Sachs assessment added a fresh estimate to China’s easing debate. Chief China economist Hui Shan put year-on-year GDP growth early in Q3 at about 4%, down from 4.3% in the preceding quarter and below Beijing’s 4.5% to 5% annual target. She described July’s weakness in industrial output, consumption and investment as demand-driven. Macquarie estimated growth near 4.2%, while BNP Paribas put it at 4.1%; the latter said a pace around or below 4% through August and September, even with greater fiscal effort, could jeopardize the annual target and prompt new stimulus in late September or early October.

Those are economists’ estimates, not a new official GDP release. They nevertheless distinguish the latest assessment from the earlier observation that July activity was weak. Goldman reported some increase in market expectations of monetary easing, while noting that China’s emphasis on technology and manufacturing may do less to lift household income and consumption. Higher oil prices and factory-gate inflation had previously led many analysts to withdraw rate-cut calls. The July median analyst forecast still anticipated no policy-rate reduction this year or next; a Q4 cut in banks’ reserve requirements was viewed as more likely. Officials have so far discussed loan subsidies and other targeted financing support rather than a broad easing move.

Emerging-market returns provided another perspective on the dollar’s recent weakness. A Bloomberg gauge of eight major EM currencies has returned about 22% since the end of 2024, and dollar-funded carry trades have posted positive returns for seven consecutive quarters, their longest such run since 2008. The currency contribution varies sharply. Colombia combined high interest income with substantial peso appreciation, while yields above 32% on 10-year Turkish local bonds kept investors in profit despite a 26% decline in the lira against the dollar. Those comparisons describe a multi-quarter trade, rather than a response to Friday’s Treasury move.

The vulnerability is a firmer U.S. policy path that lifts the dollar and erodes returns earned in local currencies. Friday’s rise in the 2-year Treasury yield made that risk more immediate even as the Dollar Index finished the week lower. Goldman Sachs strategist Kamakshya Trivedi judged that high real rates could continue supporting EM currencies if U.S. long-yield moves were not too rapid. Others warned that crowded positions could amplify a reversal. The finding helps explain why a modest daily dollar decline can matter to global bond returns without implying that all EM sovereign or credit risks are improving together.

North American trade relations also deteriorated after the U.S. bond-market cutoff. U.S.-Canada talks broke down Friday night, and Washington imposed 50% tariffs on billions of dollars of Canadian goods. Prime Minister Mark Carney subsequently said Canada would apply counter-tariffs to $20 billion of U.S. products starting September 8. The later developments cannot explain Friday’s Treasury close. They add a trade and price risk to the coming week’s assessment of growth and inflation on both sides of the border.

## Forward Market Significance

Bessent’s Monday presentation is the nearest test of the distinction investors made this week between debt management and fiscal repair. Specific, durable changes to spending, revenue or projected borrowing would give the expanded buybacks a fiscal counterpart. More purchases or a different maturity mix could affect long-bond supply, but would leave the total financing requirement in place unless the promised initiative changes the deficit path. The administration’s accompanying plan to isolate Iran economically presents a separate test through oil exports, payments and shipping: Brent ended Friday at $94.39 despite Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s call to end the war.

Wednesday’s U.S. personal-consumption-expenditures report will bear on the split between Friday’s higher real yields and lower breakevens. Economists expect the July headline price index to rise 3.6% from a year earlier, which would be the smallest annual gain in four months, and expect little change in inflation-adjusted personal spending. The composition will matter to a Fed weighing strong business activity against softer labor and consumer evidence. Revised Q2 GDP is also due Wednesday, with July new-home sales on Tuesday and a preliminary payrolls benchmark revision on Friday.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s first Jackson Hole keynote as chair on Friday is the larger policy event. Investors will look for his assessment of persistent inflation, the role of elevated long yields in restraining the economy, and how the Fed uses market signals while Treasury changes the supply of duration. Kashkari’s Sunday comments established one dissenter’s view that the bond market is functioning and that September remains data-dependent. Warsh’s explanation of the central bank’s broader reaction function could affect both the expected policy path and the uncertainty premium on longer Treasuries.

The Bank of Korea decides Thursday after the export surge, while Japan’s budget requests begin to reveal how spending will be presented under a larger initial plan and a separate investment framework. China’s subsequent activity data will test whether the roughly 4% growth pace estimated by Goldman persists despite targeted fiscal support. In credit, Braskem’s August 24 stay deadline can turn nonbinding proposals into an agreed negotiating route or a court-led process. Across AI finance, the next large project and hyperscaler transactions will show whether crossover demand continues to absorb supply at current yields, and whether smaller borrowers can bear the same funding cost.

Equities welcomed the growth signal, but semiconductor weakness and costly AI borrowing showed that demand for long-term capital remained a concern. European policy readings diverged, while distressed-credit outcomes depended on asset claims and rescue financing.
